chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: The Off-Beat manager who later plays him a Sarah Vaughan record
summary: Another club owner turns Sarah down, then two years later proudly plays her record, which Malachi takes as proof that owners know nothing about talent.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: But I went on trying to find some work with Sarah, and I went to another club owner who was up at Seventh and T Streets then. There was a club called the Off-Beat, and the guy that was managing it then was a guy named Tassin(?). He's got a place of business here now, I think; I think he has a restaurant and a cleaners. But then he was running a club. And I talked to him about Sarah. And he didn't use that kind of language. He just didn't have no eyes for usin' Sarah Vaughan at all. And he had also heard her.
To go off the point a little bit, about two years later,

I happened to go by the same club where he was the manager, and I walked in, and he said, "Hey, Johnny..." Everybody around here used to call me Johnny. "Hey, Johnny, come here a minute." So I went and I said, "What do you want?" He said, "Come on back in my office." I went back in his office, and he said, "Man, I got something I want you to hear." So I went back -- and he had a record player back there. He put this record on, and sat back. "See, I want you to hear this bitch sing," he says. It was Sarah Vaughan singing. And I called him all kinds of dumb so-and-so's and told him, "Man, this is the girl that I tried to bring in here to sing."

Which shows you that the club-owners don't know their ass from a hole in the ground as far as entertainment is concerned. And this is true with a whole lot of people that are running clubs. They are liquor salesmen, and that's all. As far as entertainers and musicians are concerned, they know absolutely nothing! Anyway, that was just an incident that I thought of to bring out to show you that the things that an artist has to go through with... Sometimes, the greater the artist, the worse the situation can be.
